hotspots.label: RIVER SYSTEM

hotspots.label: JAGUAR
hotspots.detail: The journey remains anchored to canonical Jaguar identity while the relationship layer expands.

hotspots.label: CAPYBARA
hotspots.detail: A relationship node from the shared SPECIES relationship contract. Open HOW DO WE KNOW? for the source and boundary.

hotspots.label: WATER
hotspots.detail: Water is shown as spatial context around the relationship. Co-location alone is not presented as causation.

items.label: Next move
items.note: Pull back from animal to habitat

habitat.title: The animal is not the whole story.
habitat.body: Pull back. Rivers, floodplain forest, canopy and movement corridors turn one species encounter into a living-system view.

hotspots.label: RIVER SYSTEM
hotspots.detail: The river is a spatial organising feature in this scene. No water-quality condition is inferred from the image.

hotspots.label: FLOODPLAIN FOREST
hotspots.detail: A habitat concept layer used to help the user see the wider system around the animal.

hotspots.label: UPPER CANOPY
hotspots.detail: The canopy is presented as part of the living place, not as a measured biodiversity inventory for this exact view.

hotspots.label: RIPARIAN CORRIDOR
hotspots.detail: Connectivity is a product concept here. Any local corridor claim requires mapped evidence before publication.

hotspots.label: SOIL NETWORK
hotspots.detail: A prompt to explore below-ground relationships later. No species or process is asserted from this scene alone.

items.label: Animal
items.note: One entrance into a larger system

items.label: ATLAS
items.note: Spatial inspection stays on the shared map engine

pressure.title: Now the landscape changes.
pressure.body: See fragmentation as a change in the system, then inspect what the evidence actually supports before moving to response.

hotspots.label: FRAGMENTATION
hotspots.detail: The Journey uses fragmentation as the pressure concept. The scene must not be read as a live or exact quantitative condition map.

hotspots.label: LAND CONVERSION
hotspots.detail: Land conversion is a documented Amazon pressure category. Local attribution requires place- and time-specific evidence.

hotspots.label: ROADS + ACCESS
hotspots.detail: Infrastructure can open new access, but no percentage or local causal contribution is asserted in this prototype frame.

hotspots.label: EVIDENCE
hotspots.detail: Use the Journey evidence control for the exact source record and limitation attached to this node.

items.label: Occurrence
items.note: Never treated as range or population

items.label: Pressure
items.note: Sourced category; local magnitude not inferred

response.title: Pressure is not the destination.
response.body: Move from problem intelligence into response pathways. These are solution classes and actor roles — not claims that 4PLANET has selected, funded or delivered them.

hotspots.label: RESTORE
hotspots.detail: Restoration can be explored as a response class. Delivery effectiveness depends on ecology, governance, permanence and local stewardship.

hotspots.label: PROTECT
hotspots.detail: Protection is a pathway class, not a generic outcome claim. A real project requires an accountable actor and evidence.

hotspots.label: MONITOR
hotspots.detail: Monitoring can strengthen evidence and accountability. Monitoring alone is not ecological recovery.

hotspots.label: LOCAL STEWARDSHIP
hotspots.detail: Local and Indigenous stewardship is represented as an actor-role category only. No partnership or endorsement is implied.

items.label: Solution intelligence
items.note: Compare response classes, evidence and fit

items.label: Actor intelligence
items.note: Role classes only until organisations are verified

items.label: Action
items.note: No impact claim before delivery evidence
